title: Metronome shift notes - kernel triage & microbatch TODOs
content:
Context:
- Night shift catch-up: intermittent p99 spikes around 40s window for small requests (len<=64) on 3090 pools.
- Observed pattern: bursty arrival from a particular customer (customer-b) correlates with microbatch windows aligning -> large batch assembly + kv-cache cold misses.

Raw observations (logs + quick grep):
- 2026-03-10T22:11:13Z host-gpu-12: request len=28 arrived, queued 37ms, batched into batch_size=48 -> kernel time ~146ms/token -> tail blowup when many small requests hit aligned step boundary.
- KV cache hit-rate for that customer dropped from 92% -> 54% during the spike window. Might be separate eviction churn.
- p99 for small requests increased from 220ms -> 1.2s in the window (not constant).

Hypotheses:
1) Microbatch alignment effect: our batching window (8ms) + continuous batching policy occasionally syncs across many clients leading to big batches that overrun our per-request latency SLO.
2) KV cache eviction thrash when multiple models share the same allocation on the 3090 pool; noise from one noisy tenant causes cold misses for others.
3) Kernel code path fallback for long key-value memory path triggers a slower GEMM kernel on specific sequence shapes.

Quick reproduction plan (local):
- Spin up 3090-sim container with workload generator (see scripts/perf/generate-burst.py).
- Recreate aligned burst: send 200 small requests at t=0 with arrival jitter <1ms.
- Commands:
  - python scripts/perf/generate-burst.py --concurrency 200 --len 32 --burst --target host-gpu-12
  - sudo perf record -F 99 -g -p <pid-of-runtime> -- sleep 20
  - nvprof --profile-from-start off --log-file nvprof.txt -- <run-binary> (if repro on baremetal)

Immediate mitigations to try (cheap, short-term):
- Lower batching window on affected pool to 4ms for canary -> reduces chance of big alignment. (config: pool/3090/continuous_batch_window_ms)
- Pin heavy tenants to separate pool temporarily until we fix eviction behavior.
- Force prefix-caching for customer-b sessions (if they’re stable clients) so KV hits improve.

Longer-term fixes and experiments:
- Evaluate jittered microbatch start: add a small random jitter (0-3ms) per request to desync alignment. Pros/cons: reduces alignments but increases scheduling variance.
- Improve KV eviction policy: switch from LRU-window to size-aware LFU-ish scoring for tokens from active sessions.
- Investigate kernel selector heuristics: when sequence_len<=64 and batch_size>40, prefer fast-small-seq kernels even if they use slightly more memory; add benchmark to compile-time guard.

Open tasks (tracked in JIRA):
- [INF-8734] Investigate KV eviction churn (owner: Sanjay) - collect per-tenant cache metrics for last 7 days - due 2026-03-15.
- Add microbatch jitter experiment (owner: Irene) - deploy to canary 3090-pool and run synthetic burst test - due 2026-03-13.
- Kernel selector benchmark (owner: Maya) - extend benchmark harness to include shapes (seq<=64, batch>=40) and record kernel timings - due 2026-03-18.

Quick notes to self (small TODOs):
- Add log line for batch-assembly event: include first_request_ts and alignment_offset_ms. (cheap)
- Push a small feature flag to flip continuous_batch_window_ms at runtime.
- Check if autoscaler burst policy interacted with request routing (did we suddenly move traffic between machines?).

Hypothesis test plan for microbatch jitter (experiment steps):
1) Canary config: continuous_batch_window_ms=6 -> add jitter_ms=random(0,3) per request.
2) Run 6h synthetic window that sends burst patterns matching production.
3) Measure: p50/p90/p99 for len<=64; KV hit-rate per tenant; batch size distribution.
4) If p99 drops by >=20% and batch utilization wins not >5% degrade, roll to 3090 pool.

Notes from quick kernel dive (what I saw in perf flame):
- Majority of cycles in small-batcher case are spent in copy/gather for KV cache miss path (~32%); matmul kernels accounted for ~45% as expected.
- There's a hot function in allocator code path that kicks in when batch allocation crosses a page boundary (fragmentation). Could be version bump candidate for allocator tuning.

Commands/snippets I want to keep handy:
- tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/runtime/runtime.log | grep 'batch-assembled' --context=3
- python tools/kv_inspect.py --tenant customer-b --since 2026-03-08 --output csv
- kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=3090 -o wide

Decisions to propose in Monday sync:
- Try jitter canary + pin noisy tenants to soft-isolated pool for one week. If KV thrash persists, move to hard isolation.
- Add a short-term patch to expose continuous_batch_window_ms as runtime flag in agent to allow fast rollback.

Final quick checklist for today:
- [ ] Deploy jitter canary to 1 pod in 3090 pool (Irene)
- [x] Ask infra to pin customer-b to soft-isolation (Sanjay)
- [ ] Add batch-assembly logs (Irene)
- [ ] Start kernel microbenchmark for small-seq shapes (Maya)

Notes-to-self overflow:
- If tempted to change default batch window globally, don't — causes user-visible latency variance. Always canary.
- Remember to sync with SRE about alert thresholds: current p99 alert flips during SLO window too often and is noisy.

End of notes.
